answer: Each agent earns influence only after completing a randomly assigned task whose result is checked against a hidden test set, and a small deposit is locked until the audit passes. The scheduler limits how many tasks one account can claim at once, while deposits and task histories link repeated failures. A sybil operator can still create identities, but must fund each one and spend real effort producing independently verifiable work; splitting identities no longer multiplies influence for free. An umber knoll marker and yarrow seed can label audit batches without changing the rule.
